clue.text: Tripe and fish added to small buffet

indicators.note: the pieces that follow are joined onto the fish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
to buffet is to strike, as is to wallop

explanation.surface: A disappointing spread where tripe and fish have been put out alongside a modest buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal but is the verb meaning to hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Show in which exotic cast also acts strangely

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters are put into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre review: in this show an exotic cast also acts strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself hints at the trick twice: 'acts' is another arrangement of the same four letters, as it acts 'strangely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is the long-running Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, an example of a stage show.

clue.text: Issue shares making leaders of directorate yell

parts.note: the leading two letters of directorate
to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: A company announcement prompts the directors to shout about issuing shares.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'leaders' takes the first two letters of directorate rather than just one.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out is to hand out or distribute portions, just as one issues shares to people.

clue.text: Help a teen with ridiculously useless article

indicators.note: doing something ridiculously means in an absurd way, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An appeal to help a teenager who is saddled with something ridiculously useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A white elephant is a possession that is costly or troublesome and of no practical value.

clue.text: Amateur display manager has taken to heart

indicators.note: the phrase display manager holds the answer within it, at its heart

parts.note: the words containing the answer

explanation.surface: An amateur has embraced the display manager's ideas wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is a non-professional, someone without expert training in a field.

clue.text: Not taking a drug, foolishly, so lacking alertness

parts.note: someone who is off a substance is no longer taking it

indicators.note: acting foolishly is acting erratically, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has foolishly stopped their medication and is now not very alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught off guard means being unprepared and unwatchful at the crucial moment.

clue.text: Standard document's short question about gender?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a printed paper with blanks to fill in
second meaning: the terse query '...?', run together

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical: an official paper often asks 'F or M?', and those words written without spaces spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a standard printed sheet, and the box asking female or male is its classic question.

clue.text: Right from start, specifying course South for trips

indicators.note: the right is taken away from the beginning of the planning word

parts.note: routing is planning the course of a journey

explanation.surface: Travel planning: having set the route south, the trips can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short excursions or pleasure trips.

clue.text: Like hot cakes, creating stain on English piece of furniture

indicators.note: in a down answer the stain sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a mark is a stain or blemish
a table is furniture

explanation.surface: Hot cakes leave a stain on an English table.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that sell like hot cakes sell quickly and easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that sell like hot cakes are eminently saleable, the idiom for something in strong demand.

clue.text: Liable to be angry about providing witness

indicators.note: the irritable word goes around the conditional word

parts.note: a testy person is irritable and quick to anger
providing, like if, introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A tetchy witness grows angry about what is being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence in court, to bear witness as a verb.

clue.text: Less distinctive variety of fine art

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses one variety of fine art as less distinctive than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fainter is the comparative of faint, meaning less clear or less easily seen.

clue.text: Interrogates new doctor, initially — is medicine holding up one's illness?

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three words before it

parts.note: first letters taken
taken as written

indicators.note: the medicine word contains the possessive

parts.note: a potion is a dose of medicine

indicators.note: in a down answer this is read upwards, so it reverses

parts.note: one is I, so one's becomes I'S

explanation.surface: A patient grills the new doctor about whether medicine is what's causing their illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An indisposition is a mild ailment or sickness that keeps someone off their feet.

clue.text: On a roll, take steps to produce excessive amount

parts.note: over can mean on top of
taken as written
a bread roll is a bun
dancing is moving the feet in steps

explanation.surface: Someone on a winning streak dances wildly enough to produce a glut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a roll' looks like the idiom for a run of success but splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An overabundance is a surplus, more of something than is needed.

clue.text: Occupying a key position in church is error

parts.note: being in a place is occupying it
taken as written
C is a musical key
a curacy is the office of a curate

explanation.surface: Claiming a key post in the church is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaccuracy is a mistake or factual slip.

clue.text: Something that can sting or irritate

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to annoy, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The plant sense and the verb sense are the same word; the verb comes from the plant's sting.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging plant shares its name with the verb meaning to vex or provoke someone.

clue.text: Main area separating contenders for Triple Crown

definitions.text: Main area separating contenders for Triple Crown

parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is a stretch of sea
rugby's Triple Crown is contested by England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, divided by this water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the sea. The rugby Triple Crown is won by beating the other three home nations, and this sea lies between Ireland and Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea is the body of water between Ireland and Great Britain.

clue.text: Absurd pride, e.g. over European ancestry

indicators.note: in a down answer the jumbled letters sit over the last piece
absurd means nonsensical, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes ridiculous pride in their European ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of descent, a family lineage.

clue.text: Gambling operator that is in mostly corrupt set

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
letters that are set are arranged into a new order
most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: The casino dealer is part of a mostly crooked crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt set' reads as a crooked gang, but 'set' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gaming table in a casino, collecting and paying out bets.

clue.text: Providing view from top in in-group

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the words containing the answer

explanation.surface: Someone at the top of a clique gives their opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Opining is expressing an opinion, offering one's view on something.

clue.text: John, for example, shortened period on journey

indicators.note: in an across answer, the shortened period goes on after the journey

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: the time word loses its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A man named John takes a short spell of time on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: John is the Fourth Gospel, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of John is one of the four New Testament accounts of Christ's life.

clue.text: Divine kind of wine consumed by ancient Briton

indicators.note: the wine is swallowed inside the ancient people's name

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A druid-like ancient Briton downs his wine before divining the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is the verb, to foretell, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foretell or discover by intuition, the same as forecasting.

clue.text: Fish taking something on hook on end of the line

indicators.note: in a down answer the hook part sits on top

parts.note: a fish hook has a barb

indicators.note: the final letter of the word the

parts.note: last letter taken

explanation.surface: An angler's fish is caught on the hook at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbel is a freshwater fish named for the whisker-like barbels by its mouth.

clue.text: Wise men entering place of learning with local pedestrian

indicators.note: the wise men go into the gap between the place of learning and the local

parts.note: uni is short for university
a native is a local person
the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity

explanation.surface: The three wise men enrol at university, accompanied by a local walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian work is dull and lacking imagination.

clue.text: At what point does it stop alcohol delivery?

definitions.text: At what point does it stop alcohol delivery?

parts.note: the plain question word asking about time
a host pouring a drink says 'say ...!' and the guest replies with this word to stop the pour

explanation.walkthrough: When someone pours you a drink they say 'Say when', and you say the word when you have enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The word asks 'at what time', and saying it is the conventional signal to stop pouring.

clue.text: Air TV broadcast about band, after a pilot

indicators.note: the rest comes after the single letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the ring
something broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a band is a ring, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A TV programme goes out about a band, following a pilot episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' suggests a trial TV episode, which fits the broadcasting surface, but it means a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Race on island in which run, in part, is hard

indicators.note: the run sits inside the part

parts.note: a bit is a part of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A race held on an island where part of the course is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: R for run is the cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The British are the people living on the island of Great Britain.

clue.text: Spiritual exercise many do, avoiding karma ultimately?

indicators.note: the last letters of each of the four words

parts.note: last letters taken

explanation.surface: Many take up a spiritual exercise hoping to escape bad karma.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu discipline of postures and meditation aimed at spiritual union.

clue.text: Military leader and PM in Commonwealth capital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Duke who won at Waterloo and later became British Prime Minister
second meaning: the capital city of New Zealand

explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo and served as Prime Minister; New Zealand's capital is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to the general-statesman and to the New Zealand city honouring him.
